_doc: The Annals (systems/annals.js): the story of the player's life and dynasty, told from what the systems already record — the House chronicle (house.history), the reign records (house.reigns, systems/legacy.js), the wealth marks (house.wealthMarks), traits, sagas, achievements, fame, lords' memories and the ledger. Every phrase list here is picked by a hash of (event, day) — never the shared RNG — so the same save always reads the same. Tokens in {braces} are filled by the composer; {Pronoun}/{pronoun}/{poss}/{obj} follow the ruler's gender. `tagWeights` decide what is notable: an entry's weight is the highest of its tags' weights, and only entries at or above `minWeight` make the book (a chapter with fewer than `minEvents` takes its best lesser entries too). `themes` map tags to the book's themes (first match wins).
_rewrites: Chronicle lines written as bare noun phrases, made into sentences: [pattern, replacement]; {name} is the ruler, $1.. the captures.
rewrites: {name} gained a claim on the throne of $1.

pastTense._doc: The book is written in the past: chronicle lines (house.history; most are written in the present, 'Bran weds Tamsin.') are put into the past tense after `rewrites`. `phrases` first ([regex, replacement], each applied everywhere), then `words` (whole lowercase words). A word that is too often a noun ('lies', 'rules', 'claims', 'returns') goes in `phrases` with its context instead. Text inside quotes is left alone.

founder: In the {season} of the year {year}, {name} set {poss} name to a new House, and {house} entered the annals.
The annals of {house} begin in the {season} of the year {year}, with {name}, aged {age}, and not much else.
It was the {season} of the year {year} when {name} first called {obj}self of {house}. {Pronoun} was {age} years old.
stranger: {name} was {station} of {town} when the old line ended, and in the {season} of the year {year} began a new House: {house}.
Out of {town} came {name}, {station}, aged {age}, to found {house} in the year {year}.
heir: In the {season} of the year {year}, {name} took up the mantle of {house}, aged {age}.
The year {year} gave {house} a new head: {name}, {age} years old.
{name} came to the head of {house} in the {season} of the year {year}, at the age of {age}.

openingDisputed: Not every voice in the House agreed{quelled}.
openingRegency: A regency held the House in {poss} name until {pronoun} came of age.
traitEarned: It was in these days that {name} was first called {trait}.
By now the talk in the taverns named {name} {trait}.
overflow: Of lesser matters that year the annals keep {n} more.
And {n} lesser matters besides, which the scribes did not think worth the ink.
quietYears: The years {from} to {to} passed quietly, and the annals keep little of them.
Of the years between {from} and {to} the scribes wrote little.
For {n} years after, the annals fall quiet.
achievement: The heralds cried a new honour for {name}: "{deed}".
The bards made a song of it, and called it "{deed}".
"{deed}", the heralds named the deed of {name}.
saga: The tale of {saga} came to its end: {title}. {name} had a hand in it{won}.
So ended {saga}: {title}. {name} was part of that story{won}.

war: The tally of {poss} wars: {battles} battle{battlesS} won{settlementsClause}.
summary.warSagas: {beasts} beast{beastsS} of legend fell to {poss} hand.
rise: {name} gained {titles} office{titlesS} and {prestige} Prestige for the House.
The House rose under {obj}: {titles} office{titlesS} won, {prestige} Prestige gained.
riseLost: The House's standing fell under {obj}: {prestige} Prestige lost.
It was not a reign that raised the House: {prestige} Prestige lost.
summary.crownLost: The crown of {crown} was {how} after {days} days.
justice: {name} sat in judgement {ruled} time{ruledS}; the rulings remembered: {rulings}.
Of the {ruled} petition{ruledS} {name} heard, these were remembered: {rulings}.
wealthRange: {name} came to the House's purse with {start} gold and left it with {end}.
The coffers held {start} gold when {name} took them and {end} at the last.
wealthPeak: At the height of {poss} fortune, in the year {year}, {name} counted {peak} gold.
The fortune peaked in the year {year}, at {peak} gold.
summary.wealthLow: The lean years came in {year}, when the purse fell to {low} gold.
wealthSource: Most of the coin of late came from {source}.
Of late the House lived chiefly on {source}.
summary.wealthSpend: The heaviest spending of late was on {sink}.
familyChildren: {Pronoun} fathered a line: {names} — {count} child{childrenS} in all.
familyChildrenF: {Pronoun} mothered a line: {names} — {count} child{childrenS} in all.
summary.familyLost: Of them, {lost} did not live to see {poss} death.
faithPious: {name} was known for {poss} faith: {prayers} prayer{prayersS} and {pilgrimages} pilgrimage{pilgrimagesS}.
Few doubted {poss} faith — {prayers} prayer{prayersS} said, {pilgrimages} pilgrimage{pilgrimagesS} made.
summary.faithName: Men called {obj} {traits}, and meant it as praise.
summary.infamyCrimes: The watch knew {obj}: {crimes} crime{crimesS}, caught {caught} time{caughtS}.
summary.infamyTraits: Men called {obj} {traits}, and did not say it kindly.

closed: {name} died of {cause} in the {season} of the year {year}, aged {age}, after {years} year{yearsS} at the head of the House.
Death came for {name} in the year {year}: {cause}. {Pronoun} was {age}, and had led the House {years} year{yearsS}.
In the {season} of the year {year}, {cause} took {name}, aged {age}.
closedNoCause: {name} died in the {season} of the year {year}, aged {age}, after {years} year{yearsS} at the head of the House.
The annals mark {poss} passing in the year {year}, at the age of {age}.
abdicated: In the {season} of the year {year}, aged {age}, {name} set down the seat after {years} year{yearsS} at the head of the House.
{name} stepped down in the year {year}, at the age of {age}, and the House passed to {heir}.
abdicatedForced: In the year {year} the lords of the court made {name} set down the seat, aged {age}, after {years} year{yearsS}.
{name} was put from the seat in the {season} of the year {year}; the House passed to {heir}.
elderLives: The old ruler lives on, out of the seat.
elderDied: {Pronoun} lived on out of the seat until the year {diedYear}, when {elderCause} took {obj}, aged {diedAge}.
Retired, {pronoun} died of {elderCause} in the year {diedYear}, aged {diedAge}.
live: {name} lives still, aged {age}, in the {nth} year at the head of the House.
The annals of {name} are not yet closed: {pronoun} lives, aged {age}.

legacy.title: Legacy
headline: So stands {house}, {generations} generation{generationsS} on: {rank}.
Such is the measure of {house} after {generations} generation{generationsS}: {rank}.
ended: The line of {house} ended in the year {year} with {last}. {rank}.
With {last}, in the year {year}, the line of {house} ended. The scribes judged it {rank}.
legacy.holdingsNone: The House holds no land of its own.
wealth: The family fortune rose from {first} gold to a peak of {peak} in the year {peakYear}; it stands at {last}.
From {first} gold the purse grew to {peak} at its height (year {peakYear}), and holds {last} now.
legacy.wealthFell: From {first} gold the purse has fallen to {last}; its best was {peak}, in the year {peakYear}.
legacy.childrenNone: No child of its blood lives now.
legacy.achievements: {won} deeds sung by the bards, of {total}.

scribe.system: You are the court scribe of a medieval House, writing its annals. Rewrite the notes you are given into one chapter of flowing chronicle prose, past tense, solemn and vivid. Use ONLY the facts in the notes: never invent people, places, numbers, battles or events, and keep every name exactly as written. No headings, no lists, no preamble.

Write the chapter "{title}" from these annals:

{text}
